idea: Why a toilet may keep running
title: Why a Toilet Keeps Running: The Flapper Seal
description: A constantly running toilet is usually caused by water continuously escaping the tank, preventing the float from signaling the fill valve to shut off. In most cases, the culprit is a degraded flapper valve seal at the base of the tank. Over time, in-tank chemical cleaners and hard water minerals cause the rubber flapper to harden, warp, or accumulate scale, preventing a watertight seal against the flush valve seat. As water leaks into the bowl, the fill valve stays open to replenish it. Inspecting and replacing a compromised flapper is the most practical first step in troubleshooting a running toilet.

visual_story: The visual features a cutaway view of a toilet tank interior focusing on the rubber flapper valve at the bottom of the tank. Viewers can clearly observe how a warped rubber seal creates a gap against the flush valve seat, allowing tank water to leak continuously into the bowl. This visual helps viewers connect the sound of running water to the exact mechanical seal failure taking place inside the tank.

on_image_text.hook: Why Your Toilet Won't Stop Running
on_image_text.explanation: A warped or degraded flapper fails to seal the flush valve, letting water constantly leak into the bowl.
on_image_text.takeaway: Inspect and clean the rubber flapper seal before replacing the entire fill valve assembly.
